tools.name: search_test_cases
tools.description: Search test cases by AQL (Allure Query Language) query. PREFER find_test_cases for broad multi-field search — it automatically searches name + Suite + Feature. Use this tool for precise, targeted AQL queries when you need custom field filters or complex logic.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

rql.description: AQL (Allure Query Language) filter expression. This tool has no 'query' field — the filter goes in 'rql'. For plain keyword/name search, use find_test_cases instead. Operators: = != ~= (contains) > < >= <= in [...] and or not, plus '= null' / 'is null' for empty fields. IMPORTANT: 'not in' is written as 'not field in [...]', NOT 'field not in [...]'. IMPORTANT: 'and' has higher precedence than 'or' — parenthesize explicitly when mixing them, e.g. '(a = "x" or a = "y") and b = true'. Dates use 13-digit Unix ms timestamps. Full syntax: https://docs.qameta.io/reference/aql/ — glossary: docs/usages/aql-reference.md Test case fields: id, name, tag, issue, role["R"], member, cf["F"], cfv, layer, status, workflow, testPlan, automation (boolean), muted, mutedDate, createdDate, createdBy, lastModifiedDate, lastModifiedBy. Custom field patterns: cf["Feature"] = "keyword" | cf["Epic"] = "Auth" | cf["Suite"] = "MySuite". Examples: name ~= "login" | automation = true | automation = false | status = "Active" | tag in ["smoke", "regression"] | not tag in ["nightly"] | cf["Feature"] = "keyword" and cf["Suite"] = "MySuite" | name ~= "checkout" and muted = false | (createdBy = "a" or createdBy = "b") and automation = true

tools.name: find_test_cases
tools.description:
Broad search for test cases — use as the FIRST step before creating new test cases to check for duplicates. The "query" parameter searches test case name (contains match). Use "feature", "suite", or "customFieldFilters" to search by custom field values (exact match).

WORKFLOW (general → specific):
1. Broad search:   find_test_cases({ query: "keyword" }) — searches by test case name
2. By custom field: find_test_cases({ feature: "keyword" }) — exact match on Feature custom field
3. Combined:       find_test_cases({ query: "login", feature: "Auth", automated: true }) — name + filters
4. Targeted AQL:   search_test_cases({ rql: 'cf["Feature"] = "keyword" and automation = false' }) — precise query

At least one of the search/filter parameters must be provided.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

query.description: Search keyword — searches test case name (contains match). Use for broad name-based discovery. To search custom fields, use the "feature", "suite", or "customFieldFilters" parameters.

name.description: Filter by test case name (contains match). Use to narrow results to a specific name pattern.

suite.description: Filter by Suite custom field value (exact match). Use to narrow results to a specific suite. NOTE: the custom field must be named "Suite" in this project — use customFieldFilters if the name differs.

feature.description: Filter by Feature custom field value (exact match). Use to narrow results to a specific feature. NOTE: the custom field must be named "Feature" in this project — use customFieldFilters if the name differs.

automated.description: Filter by automation status: true = automated tests only, false = manual tests only.

status.description: Filter by test case status (exact match, e.g. 'Active', 'Draft', 'Deprecated').

customFieldFilters.description: Additional custom field filters for granular targeting. Each filter adds an AND condition. Example: [{ fieldName: "Epic", value: "Auth" }].

exactMatch.description: If true, use exact match (=); if false/omitted, use contains match (~=). Default: false (contains). NOTE: ~= on custom fields is not officially documented and may cause 400 errors on some Allure versions.

tools.name: get_test_case
tools.description: Get a test case by ID.

id.description: Test case ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: create_test_case
tools.description:
Create a new test case (metadata only). The scenario is added afterwards, step by step.

payload fields: name (required); projectId (defaults to ALLURE_PROJECT_ID); description (what the case verifies — always fill it); precondition (preconditions text — NOT description); expectedResult (ONE overall expected result of the whole case — this is NOT the per-step expected result); statusId together with workflowId (statusId alone → 400 'workflow and status are required'; default workflow 'Default Manual' = -1, statuses -1 Draft, -2 Review, -3 Active, -4 Outdated); testLayerId (-1 Unit Tests, -2 UI Tests, -3 API Tests by default); tags [{id}|{name}] (a name creates the tag); links [{name, url}]; customFields [{customField:{id}, id|name}]; automated.

DO NOT pass scenario/steps: the API accepts payload.scenario but stores only empty step nodes (text '<empty>', no expected results, no shared steps). Workflow: create_test_case → for each step, sequentially, create_test_case_step({testCaseId, body, expectedResult}) → verify with get_test_case_steps. Precondition / test-case expected result are shown in the UI only when the project enables those sections (project property testcase.sections.*.enabled); the API stores them either way. See MCP resource allure://guides/user-flows for the full UI-equivalent flow.

tools.name: create_test_case_step
tools.description:
Add a step to a test case (new or existing) — the only correct way to build a scenario. Equivalent to pressing Enter / 'Step with expected result' in the UI scenario editor.

- body: step text (required unless sharedStepId is given).
- expectedResult (optional): one expected-result line per ';' or newline. The tool creates the step with an Expected Result container and then one child line per entry, so get_test_case_steps shows them under step.expectedResultId.
- parentId: create a nested sub-step under that step.
- sharedStepId: insert a shared step instead of body text.
- afterId / beforeId (optional): position among siblings; without them the step is appended at the end.

The response contains createdStepId (the step) and expectedResultId (its ER container, when expectedResult was given). To add expected results to an existing step use set_test_case_step_expected_result; to change text use update_test_case_step. CONCURRENCY: write steps of ONE test case sequentially (never 2+ step-writing calls for the same testCaseId in one batch) — parallel writes to the same scenario tree can silently drop a line. Different testCaseIds are safe to parallelize. See MCP resource allure://guides/user-flows for the full UI-equivalent flow.

testCaseId.description: Test case ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

body.description: Step body text. Required unless sharedStepId is provided.

expectedResult.description: Expected result for the new step. Multiple lines: separate with ; or newlines — each becomes its own ER line.

parentId.description: Parent step ID for nested steps.

sharedStepId.description: Shared step ID to reference an existing shared step instead of providing body text.

afterId.description: Insert the new step right after this sibling step ID.

beforeId.description: Insert the new step right before this sibling step ID.

tools.name: set_test_case_step_expected_result
tools.description:
APPEND expected-result lines to an existing step. If the step has no expected result yet, the Expected Result container is created first (the UI's 'Convert to → Step with expected result'); existing lines are kept and the new ones are added after them.

stepId may be the step itself or its Expected Result container. body is optional — the current step text is used when omitted.
To REPLACE all expected-result lines use update_test_case_step({testCaseId, stepId, expectedResult}). To add a step together with its expected result use create_test_case_step({..., expectedResult}). Multiple lines: separate with ; or newlines. CONCURRENCY: write steps of ONE test case sequentially (never 2+ step-writing calls for the same testCaseId in one batch) — parallel writes to the same scenario tree can silently drop a line. Different testCaseIds are safe to parallelize.

stepId.description: Step ID (or its Expected Result container ID).

testCaseId.description: Test case ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

body.description: Optional new step text; the current text is kept when omitted.

expectedResult.description: Expected result text to append. Separate multiple lines with ; or newlines.

tools.name: update_test_case_step
tools.description:
Update a step's text and/or REPLACE its expected result, without losing data. The tool reads the scenario first (that is why testCaseId is required) and sends exactly what the UI sends.

1. Text only — {testCaseId, stepId, body}: the existing expected result is preserved.
2. Replace expected result — {testCaseId, stepId, expectedResult: "A; B"}: ALL current ER lines are deleted and replaced by these lines (include every line you want to keep). The container is created if the step had none.
3. Both — pass body and expectedResult in ONE call.
4. Remove the expected result — expectedResult: "" (UI 'Convert to → Step').
5. Edit one ER line — {testCaseId, stepId: <line id from the container's children>, body}.
6. stepId may also be an Expected Result container: then expectedResult replaces its lines.

Read IDs with get_test_case_steps (step.expectedResultId → container; container.children → lines). CONCURRENCY: write steps of ONE test case sequentially (never 2+ step-writing calls for the same testCaseId in one batch) — parallel writes to the same scenario tree can silently drop a line. Different testCaseIds are safe to parallelize.

testCaseId.description: Test case ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

stepId.description: Step ID to update. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

body.description: New step text. Omit to keep the current text.

expectedResult.description: FULL replacement of the expected result (lines separated by ; or newlines). "" removes it. Omit to keep the current expected result.

tools.name: delete_test_case_step
tools.description: Delete a scenario step (UI: step menu → Delete). Deletion cascades: the step's expected result and nested sub-steps are deleted too and cannot be restored. Can also delete a single expected-result line (pass the line's id from the container's children). Returns the updated scenario.

stepId.description: Step (or expected-result line) ID to delete.

tools.name: update_test_case
tools.description:
Partially update test case metadata (only the fields you pass are changed): name, description, precondition, expectedResult (test-case level, not per-step), statusId (+ workflowId), testLayerId, automated, links, tags, customFields.

FULL REPLACE fields: links, tags and customFields replace the whole list — pass every item you want to keep (for incremental tag changes use add_test_case_tags_bulk / remove_test_case_tags_bulk; for custom fields use set_test_case_custom_fields).
NEVER pass scenario: the API replaces the WHOLE scenario with empty step nodes (all step texts and expected results are lost). Edit steps with create_test_case_step / update_test_case_step / delete_test_case_step.

id.description: Test case ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_test_case_steps
tools.description: Read the manual scenario of a test case (the same tree the UI renders). Response: root.children = ordered top-level step IDs; scenarioSteps = flat map id → step. A step has body, optional children (nested sub-steps), optional sharedStepId (inserted shared step — read its content with get_shared_step_steps), optional attachmentId (attachment node), and optional expectedResultId → the Expected Result CONTAINER node; the container's children are the expected-result lines. _meta.expectedResultWrapperIds lists all containers; _meta.regularStepIds lists the rest. Use these IDs with update_test_case_step / set_test_case_step_expected_result / delete_test_case_step. The response cache is cleared on every write. See MCP resource allure://guides/user-flows for the full UI-equivalent flow.

tools.name: update_test_result
tools.description: Update fields of a test result. payload needs only the fields to change; the current result is fetched and merged before the PATCH (the API requires the full object). Effective PATCH fields: tags, links (verified), members, customFields, testLayerId. name / description / precondition of a result linked to a test case are taken from the test case and are NOT changed by PATCH — edit the test case (update_test_case) instead. status / message / trace / categoryId are NOT part of the PATCH contract — when present they are applied through resolve (same as resolve_test_result, run steps preserved). A result that is already resolved cannot get a new status: rerun it in the UI (Rerun manually) to get a fresh in-progress result.

tools.name: resolve_test_result
tools.description:
Finish a manual test result — the UI's Passed / Failed buttons. payload: status (required: passed, failed, broken, skipped, unknown), message (failure reason), trace, categoryId, start/stop/duration (ms), execution.

Run steps: if payload.execution is omitted, the current execution (steps of the run) is read and sent back unchanged, so nothing is lost. To record per-step statuses, read the execution yourself (the steps array returned by the API for this result), set steps[i].status (and nested steps / expectedResultSteps), and pass payload.execution = {status, steps}.

Only results that are still in progress can be resolved. For an already resolved result the API answers 202 but keeps the old status — rerun the test (UI: Rerun manually) and resolve the new result. Typical manual run: create_launch → add_test_cases_to_launch → list_test_results → assign_test_result → resolve_test_result → close_launch. See MCP resource allure://guides/user-flows.

id.description: Test result ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_test_result_retries
tools.description: Get the retry history for a test result. Returns the list of previous attempts for the same test in the same launch. Key tool for flaky test detection: if a test failed on attempt 1 but passed on attempt 2, it is a flaky test, not a real failure. Check status across retries to assess reliability.

id.description: Test result ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

id.description: Test result ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_test_result_attachment_content
tools.description: Download the binary content of a test result attachment. Returns base64-encoded content with its MIME type. Use attachment ID from list_test_result_attachments. For text-based attachments (logs, JSON, XML): decode base64 to read the content. For images (screenshots): the base64 PNG/JPEG can be rendered directly.

tools.name: create_test_plan
tools.description:
Create a test plan (a saved set of test cases to run together). payload: name (required), projectId (defaults to ALLURE_PROJECT_ID), baseRql (AQL filter over test cases, e.g. 'tag = "smoke"'), treeSelection { inverted, leafsInclude, leafsExclude, groupsInclude, groupsExclude, path }, treeId.
Selection semantics: baseRql + treeSelection {inverted:true} with empty lists = every test case matching baseRql (what the UI sends); treeSelection {inverted:false, leafsInclude:[ids]} = exactly those test cases; with inverted:true, leafsInclude lists EXCLUDED test cases.
WARNING: { name } alone (no baseRql, no treeSelection) puts EVERY test case of the project into the plan.
The plan is a snapshot: test cases created later that match baseRql are added only after a sync (UI: Sync test cases). Run it with run_test_plan. See MCP resource allure://guides/user-flows.

tools.name: update_test_plan
tools.description: Partially update a test plan: name, baseRql, treeSelection, treeId (same semantics as create_test_plan; with inverted:true, leafsInclude lists EXCLUDED test cases). The test case count is recalculated after the update.

tools.description: Create a release (status Draft, default workflow). payload fields: name (required), dueDate (13-digit Unix ms timestamp), previousReleaseId, tags [{ name }]. projectId is not part of the documented ReleaseCreateDto, but the server needs it to place the release — this tool adds it from projectId/projectName or ALLURE_PROJECT_ID. To fill the release with test cases use update_release_test_case_selection or create_release_from_test_cases; to attach runs use add_launch_to_release.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: update_release
tools.description: Update a release. payload fields: name, dueDate, previousReleaseId, statusId, workflowId. Use list_release_statuses / list_release_workflows to resolve statusId and workflowId.

id.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: delete_release
tools.description: Delete a release by ID.

id.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_release_statistic
tools.description: Get aggregated test status counts for a release.

id.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: list_release_defects
tools.description: List defects detected within a release.

id.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: list_release_muted_results
tools.description: List muted test results within a release.

id.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_release_test_case_tree
tools.description: Browse the test case tree of a release: which test cases are in scope and their latest status. sort defaults to ["id,asc"] — the server's own default sort field is rejected (400 'unsupported sort field "name"').

id.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

path.description: Group IDs of the branch to expand.

tools.name: list_release_tags
tools.description: List tags attached to a release.

releaseId.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: set_release_tags
tools.description: Replace the tag set of a release. Accepts tag names as strings or { id, name } objects. This REPLACES all existing tags — read list_release_tags first and send the merged list to append.

releaseId.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: add_launch_to_release
tools.description: Attach a launch to a release so its results count towards the release statistics. Returns a task info object — recalculation runs asynchronously.

releaseId.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

launchId.description: Launch ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: remove_launch_from_release
tools.description: Detach a launch from a release.

releaseId.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

launchId.description: Launch ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_release_test_case_selection
tools.description: Get the rule that defines which test cases belong to a release (AQL and/or tree selection). A release that never had a selection returns 404 'ReleaseTestCaseSelection not found' — that is the normal empty state, set one with update_release_test_case_selection.

releaseId.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: update_release_test_case_selection
tools.description: Change the test case scope of a release. payload fields: testCaseAql (AQL over test cases) and/or treeSelection { leafsInclude, leafsExclude, groupsInclude, groupsExclude, path, inverted }. Applied asynchronously — the response is a task info object.

releaseId.description: Release ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: create_release_from_test_cases
tools.description: Create a release and populate it from a test case selection in one call. release: { name, dueDate, previousReleaseId, tags }. selection: { leafsInclude, leafsExclude, groupsInclude, groupsExclude, treeId, filterId, search, path, inverted } — projectId and inverted=false are filled in automatically.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: list_release_statuses
tools.description: List release statuses configured for a project. Use the returned ids as statusId in update_release.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: list_release_workflows
tools.description: List release workflows configured for a project. Use the returned ids as workflowId in update_release.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_automation_chart
tools.description: Get automation trend chart data for a project (test automation coverage over time).

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

from.description: Start of time range (Unix timestamp ms). Must be a number, not a string.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

offset.description: Timezone offset in HOURS (e.g. 3 for UTC+3, -5 for UTC-5). Minutes are rejected by the API (e.g. -180 → 400).

interval.description: Time interval for grouping. One of: "hour", "day", "week", "month".

tools.name: get_tc_last_result
tools.description: Get last test result for each test case in a project.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.description: Get test case success rate analytics over time for a project.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

from.description: Start of time range (Unix timestamp ms). Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: create_dashboard
tools.description: Create a new dashboard in a project. Pass payload.templateId to get ready-made widgets (templateId -1 = the 'Automation' template from the UI); without it the dashboard is empty.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

shared.description: Whether the dashboard is shared with the project.

tools.name: get_dashboard
tools.description: Get a dashboard by ID.

id.description: Dashboard ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: update_dashboard
tools.description: Update dashboard fields (name, shared status, etc.).

id.description: Dashboard ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: delete_dashboard
tools.description: Delete a dashboard by ID.

id.description: Dashboard ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: copy_dashboard
tools.description: Copy an existing dashboard (with its widgets) to the same or another project. preserveWidgetAql (default true) keeps the widgets' AQL filters in the copy.

id.description: Source dashboard ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

projectId.description: Target project ID (defaults to source project).

preserveWidgetAql.description: Keep widget AQL filters in the copy (default true).

tools.name: get_widget_data
tools.description: Get the data of a dashboard widget for a date range (the same request the dashboard page makes). Range: dateFrom / dateTo as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive); without them the server uses its default period (last 14 days). from / to (Unix ms) are still accepted and converted to dates. offset = timezone offset in HOURS (e.g. 3 or -3). page/size apply to list widgets.

id.description: Widget ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

from.description: Alternative to dateFrom: start as Unix timestamp ms (converted to a UTC date).

to.description: Alternative to dateTo: end as Unix timestamp ms (converted to a UTC date).

offset.description: Timezone offset in hours, e.g. 3 for UTC+3.

tools.name: get_defect
tools.description: Get a defect by ID. Returns the defect name, description and closed flag. Its automation rules (matchers) are separate: use find_similar_failures({launchId, defectId}) to apply them to a launch.

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: create_defect
tools.description: Create a defect that groups a failure pattern. payload: name (required), projectId (required), description (markdown), matcher (optional automation rule, the UI's 'Create automation rule'): { name (required), messageRegex, traceRegex } — results whose error message / stack trace match are auto-linked by apply_defect_matchers. linkIssue (optional, needs an issue-tracker integration): { integrationId, name }.

payload.description: Required: name, projectId. Optional: description, matcher {name, messageRegex, traceRegex}, linkIssue {integrationId, name}.

tools.name: update_defect
tools.description: Partially update a defect: name, description, closed. Close one defect: { closed: true }; reopen: { closed: false } (the same request the UI's Close/Reopen menu sends). For several defects use bulk_close_defects / bulk_reopen_defects.

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_defect_test_results
tools.description: Get the test results grouped under a specific defect. Use this to see how many failures belong to this defect and in which launches they appeared.

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_defect_test_cases
tools.description: Get the test cases affected by a specific defect. Use this to understand which test scenarios are impacted by the failure pattern.

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_defect_launches
tools.description: Get launches in which a specific defect has appeared. Use this to understand the blast radius: is this defect appearing in every run or only in specific environments?

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_launch_defects
tools.description: Get all defects present in a specific launch. This is the fastest way to get a defect summary for a launch: 'what are all the distinct failure patterns in this test run?'

id.description: Launch ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: find_similar_failures
tools.description: Find test results in a launch whose error message and/or stack trace match a regex — the same matching defect automation rules use. launchId is required. Give messageRegex and/or traceRegex directly, or give defectId to reuse that defect's automation rules (its first matcher with a regex is used). Returns matching results (id, name, message, status) — candidates for link_defect_to_test_results.

launchId.description: Launch ID to search in (required by the API).

messageRegex.description: Java regex matched against the failure message, e.g. ".*Timeout.*".

traceRegex.description: Java regex matched against the stack trace.

defectId.description: Take the regex from this defect's automation rule when messageRegex/traceRegex are not given.

tools.name: link_defect_to_test_results
tools.description: Link test results of ONE launch to a defect (UI: Link defect). Arguments: defectId, testResultIds, launchId (the launch the results belong to — required by the API), projectId/projectName (optional). The values may also be nested in `payload` (older calling convention).

testResultIds.description: Test result IDs (all from the same launch).

launchId.description: Launch ID the test results belong to.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: bulk_close_defects
tools.description: Close several defects at once (UI: Defects → select → Bulk actions → Close). Arguments: ids (defect IDs), projectId/projectName (optional, defaults to the configured project). For a single defect update_defect({id, payload:{closed:true}}) is equivalent.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: bulk_reopen_defects
tools.description: Reopen several closed defects at once (UI: Bulk actions → Reopen). Arguments: ids (defect IDs), projectId/projectName (optional).

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: link_issue_to_defect
tools.description: Link a tracker issue to a defect. payload: { integrationId (required — an issue-tracker integration connected to the project), name (required — issue key, e.g. "JIRA-123") }. Without an integration the API answers 409 'integrationId must not be null'.

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: unlink_issue_from_defect
tools.description: Remove the external issue link from a defect record.

id.description: Defect ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: apply_defect_matchers
tools.description: Apply all configured defect matcher rules to a launch. This auto-triages unresolved test results by matching them to existing defect records based on error message patterns. Run this after a launch completes to auto-group failures.

id.description: Launch ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_shared_step
tools.description: Get a shared step by ID. Returns metadata: name, project, archived status.

id.description: Shared step ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_shared_step_steps
tools.description: Get the full normalized scenario (list of steps) inside a shared step. This is the key tool for resolving sharedStepId references in test case scenarios: when get_test_case_steps returns a step with sharedStepId, call this tool to inline the actual step content. Returns the same NormalizedScenarioDto format as get_test_case_steps.

id.description: Shared step ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_shared_step_usage
tools.description: Get the list of test cases that use a specific shared step. Use this for impact analysis before editing or archiving a shared step: shows which test cases would be affected.

id.description: Shared step ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: create_shared_step
tools.description: Create a new, EMPTY shared step in a project. payload: name (required), projectId (required). This toolset cannot add steps inside a shared step yet (the UI does it in the shared step editor) — create the content in the UI, then reuse it in test cases with create_test_case_step({testCaseId, sharedStepId}). Read its content with get_shared_step_steps and its usage with get_shared_step_usage.

payload.description: Shared step creation data. Required fields: name, projectId.

tools.name: update_shared_step
tools.description: Update shared step metadata (name, etc.) by ID.

id.description: Shared step ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: archive_shared_step
tools.description: Archive a shared step to retire it from active use. Archived steps remain readable but are hidden from the active library. Run get_shared_step_usage first to check impact before archiving.

id.description: Shared step ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: unarchive_shared_step
tools.description: Restore an archived shared step back to active status.

id.description: Shared step ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: suggest_env_vars
tools.description: Search environment variable definitions by name. Returns matching env var keys with their IDs. Use this to find the exact name of an env var key before querying values.

query.description: Partial env var name to search for.

tools.name: suggest_env_var_values
tools.description: Search for recorded environment variable values by partial text. Optionally scope by envVarId, projectId, or launchId. Use this to autocomplete valid values for AQL ev[] filters before running a search.

query.description: Partial value text to search for.

envVarId.description: Filter by specific env var key ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

launchId.description: Scope to a specific launch. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: list_env_var_schemas
tools.description: List environment variable schema definitions for a project. Schemas define which env var keys are tracked and displayed for launches in this project. Use this to understand what configuration context is captured per launch in a given project.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: list_env_var_values
tools.description: List all recorded values for a specific environment variable key. Returns the distinct values that have been used across test runs (e.g. all browser versions recorded). Use envVarId from list_env_vars. Useful for building precise AQL filters: know that ev["browser"] has values ["Chrome 123", "Firefox 115"].

envVarId.description: Environment variable ID from list_env_vars. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: get_test_result_env_vars
tools.description: Get the environment variable values recorded for a specific test result. Shows what configuration context (browser, OS, env name, build) this result ran against. Use this when investigating a failure to understand if the environment is a factor: e.g. 'does this only fail on Chrome 124 but not on Firefox?'

id.description: Test result ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

tools.name: export_test_cases_csv
tools.description:
Export test cases with Allure's native CSV export (UI: select test cases → Export → CSV, every column). The export is asynchronous: POST /api/v2/test-case/bulk/export/csv → poll GET /api/export/{id} until ready → download. Columns: allure_id, name, full_name, automated, description, precondition, expected_result, status, scenario (indented step tree with expected results and shared steps), tag, link, parameter, one column per custom field and per role. Issues are not exported (they need an integration id).
Selection: testCaseIds, or rql (resolved to ids first), or neither = every test case of the project. The CSV can be imported back in the UI (Test cases → Import → CSV). For a full project backup (JSON with scenarios, attachments, shared steps, test plans) and restore, use the CLI `allure-testops-backup dump|restore` instead of calling tools in a loop. See MCP resource allure://guides/user-flows.

projectId.description: Project ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

rql.description: AQL filter for the test cases to export, e.g. tag = "smoke".

savePath.description: Local file path to write the CSV to (directories are created). Without it the CSV text is returned inline and truncated after 50000 characters.

columnSeparator.description: CSV column separator. Default ";" (as in the UI).

tools.name: export_launch_csv
tools.description: Export every test result of a launch with Allure's native CSV export (UI: launch ⋯ → Export → CSV). Asynchronous: POST /api/export/testresult/csv → poll GET /api/export/{id} → download. Columns include status, start/stop/duration, message, test_case_id, layer, scenario, tags, links, custom fields and roles.

launchId.description: Launch ID. Must be a number (integer), not a string.

savePath.description: Local file path to write the CSV to (directories are created). Without it the CSV text is returned inline and truncated after 50000 characters.

columnSeparator.description: CSV column separator. Default ";" (as in the UI).
